question: The aim of Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) was to achieve a clean and Open Defecation Free (ODF) India by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**2nd October 2019**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) was launched on 2nd October 2014 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• The mission aimed to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management in rural areas by 2nd October 2019.
 
• It was a mass movement to clean India and honor Mahatma Gandhi's vision of a clean and hygienic country.
 
• As part of the mission, over 10 crore toilets were constructed in rural India, making significant strides toward achieving an Open Defecation Free (ODF) status.
 
• The initiative involved active participation from various stakeholders, including government bodies, NGOs, and the general public.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan Urban**

 
 
• Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Urban) was launched simultaneously with the rural counterpart to focus on urban areas.
 
• The mission aimed at ensuring cleanliness and sanitation in cities and towns across India.
 
• Key components included solid waste management, construction of individual household latrines, and public awareness campaigns.
 
• Municipalities were given targets to achieve ODF status and improve waste management systems.
 
 
 
• **Open Defecation Free (ODF) Status**
 
 
• ODF status is achieved when no one in a community defecates in the open, and all households have access to functional toilets.
 
• ODF verification involves multiple levels of assessment to ensure sustainable toilet usage and maintenance.
 
• Villages achieving ODF status contribute to improving public health and environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Solid Waste Management**
 
 
• Solid waste management involves the collection, transportation, processing, and disposal of waste materials.
 
• Effective waste management practices reduce environmental pollution and promote recycling and reuse of materials.
 
• Swachh Bharat Mission emphasized the need for proper waste segregation at the source and community participation in waste management.
 
 
 
• **Behavioral Change and Public Participation**
 
 
• A key element of the Swachh Bharat Mission was to bring about behavioral change in people regarding sanitation practices.
 
• Public participation was encouraged through awareness campaigns, community-led initiatives, and involvement of local leaders.
 
• The mission aimed to create a sense of ownership and responsibility towards maintaining cleanliness among citizens.
